text: The platform runs as one platform identity in namespace `rwb-recovery` on task queue `rwb-platform`, with the flexible-server backup window and the restore right held by the operations group for the platform administrator; the archive container `rwb-temporal-archive` is write-once for the archive period of the archived history; and the values the legacy story already fixes are kept unchanged: retention 30 days (DL26), archive lead time 7 days, the archive run at 02:00, a retry count of three and a backup window of at least 35 days.
why: The platform is described by its namespace and its work, not by an identity: Template and Rules §R4 has no platform row, so no read source names the platform login, the provisioning record of task queue `rwb-platform`, the owner of the backup and restore right, the immutability period of the archive container or the approved server and SDK release. The story cannot start its drills or its archive run without a working read, and it may not invent the values, so one assumption row carries the read and the placeholder stays wherever the value is still open (CG-B-PLT-WF-02-E2039-APP-1).
read: Architecture v5 slide 44 and the Ownership Map give the platform jobs JOB-21 and JOB-22 the owner PLT on task queue `rwb-platform` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and slide 24 makes the queue and namespace the platform's unit of isolation; the ACE recovery objectives (NFR-022, NFR-023, DL11) bound the restore and failover drills, so the flexible server keeps automated backups and point-in-time restore inside them; the archive container is write-once for at least the archive period of a history, because a manifest row is only evidence while the file it names cannot change; and the values the legacy story fixes (30 days, 7 days, 02:00, three retries, a 35-day backup window) are configuration and are not re-derived here.
confirm: Platform team with the operations group, before the SIT drills of wave 0: confirm the platform login and its grants, the task queue `rwb-platform` provisioning record, the role that holds the backup window and the restore right, the immutability period of `rwb-temporal-archive`, and the approved Temporal server and SDK release.
impact: If the read is wrong the drills and the archive run are started under the wrong identity or against a server whose backup window does not cover the recovery point objective: the restore drill would then measure a recovery the live server cannot meet, and the archive could write a file whose immutability ends before its manifest row is needed as evidence. The retention, the lead time, the 02:00 cadence and the retry count do not move, because the legacy story fixes them.

text: The resilience contract is published with no platform identity row, and the values it needs are read as the working read below until the Wave 0 Service Catalog and the parameters contract fix them.
why: The platform has no service row in Template and Rules §R4, and no read source names the archive immutability period, the retry count owner, the manifest retention or the approved release, so the contract cannot publish those values; a missing approval is treated as an assumption and the contract stays Draft (realignment v1).
read: namespace rwb-recovery; task queue rwb-platform; archive container rwb-temporal-archive with a write-once period for the archive period; retention 30 days (temporal.retention.days = 30, legacy assumed, DL26); archive lead time 7 days; the archive at 02:00 daily; three retries. The immutability period, the owner of the retry count, the manifest retention and the approved release stay placeholders.
confirm: The platform team with the operations group: confirm the platform identity and the four open values before the contract is frozen.
impact: If the values differ, the archive manifest, the retry rule and the version step check change with them and v1 is not frozen; no acceptance criterion changes.

text: The replay gate is the workflow platform's: it runs in the Temporal namespace rwb-recovery, its export is a Temporal Schedule on task queue `rwb-platform` at 01:00 in SIT only, the replay histories are SIT histories in the Blob container rwb-temporal-replay with 200 histories per workflow type and a 90-day retention, and the legacy budgets stay unchanged at 24 hours of freshness, a 10-minute gate run and a 30-day timer in under 60 seconds; the gate is pinned to the platform's workflow SDK release, at Temporal 1.30 or later because Worker Versioning needs it.
why: The story must name the export cadence, the queue, the replay store, the retention and the SDK release on Day 1, and Template and Rules §R4 has no platform row, so no read source names the platform login, the gate's pipeline identity, the retention owner or the pinned release; the namespace, the platform queue and the version floor are stated by Architecture v5 and the Temporal and Drools design, so they are adopted and the remaining values are carried unchanged from the legacy story.
read: Namespace rwb-recovery; task queue `rwb-platform`; SIT histories only; 200 histories per workflow type; export daily at 01:00 with overlap SKIP; Blob container rwb-temporal-replay with 90-day retention; 24-hour freshness limit; 10-minute gate budget; 30-day timer under 60 seconds; build ID format `<git-sha>-<build-number>`; Temporal 1.30+ for Worker Versioning; the gate has no feature flag.
confirm: Platform team and SCB IT infrastructure
impact: If the read is wrong, the Schedule cadence, the queue, the retention owner or the pinned SDK release changes in a v2 of the gate; no business value, schema or business rule changes, because the replay rule and the build ID rule are fixed.

text: The workflow platform is shared platform and the replay gate contract is fixed at status Draft on Day 1 with the following working read: namespace rwb-recovery and the task queue `rwb-platform`; SIT histories only, codec-encrypted, with no production history exported; 200 closed histories per workflow type; a 24-hour freshness limit on the newest export of a type; a 10-minute gate budget and a 60-second wall-clock bound for the 30-day timer test; a 90-day replay retention; gate 10 as the tenth pipeline check in Recovery Workbench Engineering Practices; MSG-P3-038 unchanged with its {detail} fields. The pipeline identity that runs the gate, the pinned SDK version the corpus is replayed at and the owner of the build registry stay open placeholders.
why: The contract cannot be published on Day 1 without a freshness rule, a retention, a budget, a gate number and a message, and Template and Rules §R4 gives the shared platform no service row of its own; the namespace, the task queue and the gate number are stated by Architecture v5, the Ownership Map and the legacy story, so those are adopted as the working read and the remaining values are carried from the legacy configuration unchanged.
read: Temporal namespace rwb-recovery; task queue `rwb-platform`; SIT histories only and codec-encrypted; 200 histories per workflow type; 24-hour freshness; 10-minute gate budget; 60-second wall-clock bound for the 30-day timer test; 90-day replay retention; build ID format <git-sha>-<build-number>; gate 10 in Engineering Practices; MSG-P3-038 text unchanged; the pipeline identity, the pinned SDK version and the build registry owner are open.
confirm: Platform team, the pipeline owner and SCB IT architecture, at the Wave 0 Service Catalog review
impact: If the read is wrong, the index row, the gate report and the registry answers change in a v2 contract release; no business value, schema or business rule changes.

text: The shared template platform has no service row, so the namespace record is provisioned from the following working read on Day 1: namespace `rwb-recovery`; the platform identity SY-CASEWF; one AES-GCM codec key per namespace held in Azure Key Vault with an enabled version and one previous version kept for the overlap; 30 days (720 hours) retention for a closed workflow with the archive behind it; RW-PLATADM operate, RW-AUDIT read and RW-SECADM decode under break-glass; the platform task queue is task queue `rwb-platform`. The platform login and admin base, the quotas and rate limits, the namespace certificate set beyond the frontend certificate, the key rotation period and the exact retention beyond 30 days remain open placeholders.
why: Template and Rules §R4 gives the shared platform no service row, so no source fixes the identity, the quotas, the rate limits, the certificate set, the rotation period or the retention the namespace must carry, and the 19 services' workers cannot connect on Day 1 without a namespace and a key; the namespace name, the AES-GCM codec, the Key Vault key per namespace, the 30-day retention, the three roles and the platform task queue are stated by the read sources, so those are adopted as the working read and the remaining values wait for the platform review.
read: Namespace `rwb-recovery`; platform identity SY-CASEWF; AES-GCM codec key per namespace in Azure Key Vault with a version policy and an overlap window; retention of 30 days (720 hours) for a closed workflow, archived to Blob before expiry; search attributes CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup, QueueCode as Keyword; RW-PLATADM operate, RW-AUDIT read, RW-SECADM decode under break-glass; task queue `rwb-platform` for the platform's own runs; server 1.30 or later. Open: platform login and admin base, quotas, rate limits, certificate set, key rotation period, retention beyond 30 days.
confirm: SCB IT infrastructure, the ACE platform team and security architecture at the platform infrastructure review before wave 0 exit
impact: If the read is wrong, the namespace record, the key policy and the entitlement map change in a new version of the record; the 19 workers reconnect to the same namespace name and no business value, schema or business rule changes.

text: The moved non-functional story is published as one versioned baseline record on Day 1 with the following working read: the version baseline is Temporal 1.30 or later, for Nexus and Worker Versioning; one cluster per environment with its own persistence database, a namespace per workbench and one task queue per service named for that service; deterministic workflow code with all I/O in activities and no clock, randomness, Drools, network or database call in workflow code; Continue-As-New at every stage end and at least every 28 days with a stage child under parent close policy ABANDON; Worker Versioning plus the replay gate on every build; the AES-GCM payload codec with a key in Key Vault per namespace; 30 days (720 hours) retention for closed workflows with the archive to Blob behind it; the four Keyword search attributes; the metrics and health endpoints and the Web UI behind Entra ID as the operations baseline; the availability objective of 99.9 percent in business hours and 99.5 percent outside them, with the recovery point and recovery time objectives recorded as the ACE objectives, which are open; and one conformance run per release and per environment. The supported version range, the compatibility matrix, the upgrade cadence and window and the measurement window remain open placeholders.
why: A moved non-functional story becomes a standard that a check can read, and the check cannot run on Day 1 without a version family, a topology, the code rules, the data rules and a cadence; the read sources fix the 1.30-or-later family, the five-layer topology, the deterministic rule, Continue-As-New, the codec, the retention, the attributes and the ACE objectives, while the exact range, the matrix, the cadence and the measurement window are named by no source, so those are adopted from the sources where they exist and left open where they do not.
read: Temporal 1.30 or later; one cluster per environment with its own persistence database; a namespace per workbench including `rwb-recovery`; one task queue per service and task queue `rwb-platform` for the platform's own runs; deterministic workflow code with all I/O in activities; Continue-As-New at stage ends and at least every 28 days; Worker Versioning, getVersion and the replay gate; AES-GCM codec with a key in Key Vault per namespace; retention of 30 days (720 hours) with the archive behind it; search attributes CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup, QueueCode; metrics on 9090 and health on 8080; RW-PLATADM operate, RW-AUDIT read, RW-SECADM decode break-glass; availability 99.9 percent in business hours and 99.5 percent outside them; recovery objectives = the ACE objectives (open); one conformance run per release and per environment. Open: supported range, compatibility matrix, upgrade cadence and window, measurement window.
confirm: SCB IT infrastructure, the ACE platform team and security architecture at the platform infrastructure review before wave 0 exit
impact: If the read is wrong, the baseline record is reissued as a new version and the conformance check reports against the new values; the seven consumer stories re-pin the record, and no business value, schema or business rule changes.
